entities.summary: Sheri Stewart Tepper was an American writer of science fiction, horror and mystery novels. She is primarily known for her feminist science fiction, which explored themes of sociology, gender and equality, as well as theology and ecology. Often referred to as an eco-feminist of science fiction literature, Tepper personally preferred the label eco-humanist. Some of her novels fall into the category of climate fiction, in which the changing environment of a planet affects the life of its colonists in the form of a mystery to be solved; examples include Grass (1989), Beauty (1991), A Plague of Angels (1993), The Family Tree (1997), Six Moon Dance (1998), and Singer from the Sea (1999).

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: As a prominent eco-humanist science fiction author, Sheri Tepper's works have had a significant impact on feminist and environmental discourse in North America during the late 20th century. Her novels, such as Grass (1989) and Beauty (1991), have influenced the development of climate fiction and inspired new perspectives on ecological sustainability.
